title: [WT-09] Wrappers: completion landing with a remote: fetch, push first, retry
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.2 (L4 with a remote, L9), §2.3 and §2.4 (no-remote behaviour).

Objective: with an origin, the remote's target is updated before the local one by a plain (never forced) push of a commit whose only parent is B, so a lander that lost the race retries instead of diverging.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- sync_land_target / Sync-MoeLandTarget:
  - `git fetch origin refs/heads/<target>`;
  - local equal to or ahead of the fetched tip: B = local;
  - local behind: a CAS fast-forward of the local target, then B = fetched;
  - neither: MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED and nothing moves (record failed for now; WT-11 adds the route);
  - a fetch failure prints MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED and B = local;
  - it is also called before WT-04's W creation, so W is cut from a fresh target.
- L9: `git push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/<target>` with no force flag of any kind.
  - A '!' (rejected) line retries from L4 (3 attempts total).
  - A transport failure prints the existing PUSH FAILED banner with code MOE_PUSH_FAILED and continues to the local CAS.
  - MOE_PUSH_REBASE is ignored in worktree mode.
- With no remote, the fetch and push are skipped.
- Register scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh in the Linux postflight job and worktree-landing.ps1 in the Windows jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml.

The WT-08T files (task-c12f9463b68c44a18cc460a7e9460247) are held out: ALL their cases, local and remote, must pass with no edit to them. Depends on WT-08 (task-7a4aab5e0bfa48e0978eb76506edfd57).

NOT in scope: the gate and lease (WT-10); the unlanded route (WT-11); checkpoint pushes (WT-07); board ref pushes (WT-12); docs (WT-18).

Verification: bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1)
definitionOfDone: bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh (all cases) exits 0 with scripts/tests/worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} byte-identical to WT-08T's landed version.
The ps1 twin passes all cases on a Windows seat.
grep over the worktree arm of both wrappers finds no `--force`, `-f ` or `--force-with-lease` on any push; MOE_PUSH_REBASE has no effect in worktree mode (a case or grep proves it).
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs worktree-landing.sh on Linux and worktree-landing.ps1 on Windows.
node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh exit 0; both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Contract correction from the WT-S revision after QA reject 1. Where this comment and the row's description differ, the revised docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md and this comment win.

WITHDRAWN, because QA reproduced a local/remote fork with them:
- "local equal to or ahead: B = local";
- "a fetch failure prints MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED and B = local";
- "a transport failure … continues to the local CAS".

Plan against revised §1.2, §2.2 (L4/L9/L10), §2.3 and §2.6:
- L4 (sync_land_target / Sync-MoeLandTarget):
  - Fetch with `git fetch --no-write-fetch-head origin refs/heads/<target>:refs/remotes/origin/<target>` (no `+`), up to 3 tries, MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC apart (default 5).
  - B = refs/remotes/origin/<target>, never the local target.
  - If all 3 fetches fail, nothing lands: MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED, unlanded `remote`.
  - A local target that is not an ancestor of B gives MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED. Otherwise fast-forward the local target to B.
  - W creation (WT-04) cuts from refs/remotes/origin/<target> after this fetch. If the fetch fails it uses the ref as last fetched; with no such ref at all it gives MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- L9: `git push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/<target>`, with no force flag of any kind.
  - Flag ' ', '*' or '=': published.
  - Flag '!': the round ends.
  - Anything else goes to reconcile_push / Resolve-MoePushOutcome. It waits the backoff, then repeats the fetch:
    - C contained: published.
    - fetched without C: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, and the round ends.
    - the fetch fails: the outcome is unknown.
- Unknown outcome:
  - MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and no ref moves;
  - keep the journal, with pushResult `push unknown: <detail>`;
  - put a `push-unknown` rescue ref on C;
  - send no completion row and no finalize.
- L10 mirror: an ff-only CAS of the local target to C. A refusal is MOE_LAND_MIRROR_SKIPPED and never a landing failure.
- Worktree arm of receipt_replay / Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay: fetch first, then run the unchanged receipt_landed_as against refs/remotes/origin/<target>. A failed fetch keeps the journal; it never drops it.
- `pushed: true` only after a confirmed publication.
- Exhausted rounds end as `contention`, or as `remote` when the last round ended on a transport failure.

WT-08T's `remote` cases, including the race and the unknown outcome, must pass unchanged.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Follow-up to the WT-S revision comment above. Two additions from revised §2.2 L4 and its error handling:

1. Read the local target as L BEFORE the fetch.
   - Report MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED only when that L is not an ancestor of B.
   - Why: mirrors only ever move the local target to commits the remote already held. Read this way, a peer's mirror that lands between your fetch and your check cannot fake a divergence. That matters because no lease runs when no qualityGate is set.
   - A fetch refused as non-fast-forward counts as one failed try. When a peer moved the tracking ref mid-fetch, the next try clears it.

2. Test the remote-mode W base in scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1}, since the WT-08T files stay held out.
   - W is cut from refs/remotes/origin/<target>.
   - With no such ref, expect MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
   - This row's files become 5: the two wrappers, both postflight harnesses and .github/workflows/ci.yml.

Also extend your parity grep to cover `MOE_PUSH_`.
